source.title: Neurodevelopment of the association cortices: Patterns, mechanisms, and implications for psychopathology

confidence_rationale: High-authority multimodal Neuron review establishing the sensorimotor-to-association axis of cortical maturation as a robust, evolutionarily rooted developmental program: lower-order sensory/unimodal cortices mature before higher-order transmodal association cortices, and this ordering exists precisely to enhance feature differentiation between the two. Maps cleanly onto INV-088's premise that world-feature representation (E1/z_world, sensory-like) differentiates before the goal/evaluator (E3, association/PFC-like) can be productively trained. Confidence held below 0.8 because the review evidences the maturational ordering and the differentiation-enhancement, but does not directly test the FUNCTIONAL bound (an evaluator trained on poorly-differentiated input noise-fits) that INV-088 asserts; mapping_fidelity weighted heavily as this is an architectural claim.
failure_signatures: The review documents maturational timing (sensory-before-association) and enhanced feature variation, but does not measure evaluator/value-readout quality as a function of upstream representational differentiation, so it cannot by itself confirm the strict bound (evaluator quality strictly bounded by z_world differentiation) vs merely a temporal correlation.

The same protracted association-cortex plasticity that supports the ordering is shown to confer psychopathology risk, indicating the sensory-first program is not uniformly protective -- a poorly-differentiated-but-still-plastic association stage is a documented failure mode rather than a guaranteed clean sequence.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Human cortical development proceeds hierarchically along a sensorimotor-to-association axis: primary/unimodal sensory and motor cortices mature first, higher-order transmodal association cortices (executive, socioemotional, mentalizing) mature last, and this staggered program serves to enhance feature variation between lower- and higher-order regions.
mapping.ree_translation: INV-088 asserts that the quality of E3's z_world-reading evaluators (harm_eval(z_world), benefit_eval, goal/trajectory scoring) is bounded by E1's z_world representational differentiation, so productive training of the evaluators cannot precede sufficient world-schema differentiation. The paper's sensory-before-association maturational ordering is the biological existence proof for this dependency: the world-representation (sensory-like) must differentiate before the evaluator (association/PFC-like) matures, and the differentiation gap is exactly what late association maturation exploits.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The review establishes temporal ordering and feature differentiation, not a measured functional bound. INV-088's stronger claim -- that a poorly-differentiated z_world yields a noise-fitted evaluator -- is consistent with, but not directly demonstrated by, the developmental-timing evidence. Temporal precedence is necessary but not sufficient evidence for a causal representational bound.
mapping.source_context: Human in-vivo multimodal neuroimaging (structural, functional, microstructural MRI) across childhood and adolescence; review synthesizing cross-study developmental gradients.

confidence_components.notes: Neuron flagship review, framework widely replicated. Transfer risk moderate: the sensorimotor-to-association axis is architectural/evolutionary and plausibly substrate-general, but human-neuroimaging -> REE artificial-substrate transfer plus the ordering-to-bound inferential step keep transfer_risk non-trivial.
